summary.text: Mark Takano is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for California's 39th District, first elected in 2012. A Riverside native and Harvard graduate, he taught in the Rialto Unified School District and served on the Riverside Community College District board before entering Congress. He is Ranking Member of the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs, which he previously chaired, and sits on the Education and the Workforce Committee.

paragraphs.text: Born in 1960 and raised in Riverside, California; his official biography says his grandparents and parents were removed from their homes and sent to Japanese American internment camps during World War II, and that he graduated as valedictorian of La Sierra High School in 1979.
Earned a bachelor's degree in government from Harvard College in 1983.
Began teaching in the Rialto Unified School District in 1988 and worked as a teacher at Rialto High School before his election to Congress.
Was elected to the Riverside Community College District Board of Trustees in 1990 and became board president in 1991.
Earned a Master of Fine Arts in creative writing from the University of California, Riverside in 2010.
Was elected to Congress in 2012; his official biography describes him as the first openly gay person of color elected to Congress.

Serves as Ranking Member of the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs (and its Subcommittees on Economic Opportunity and Health) and as a member of the Education and the Workforce Committee, including its subcommittees on Workforce Protections and Higher Education and Workforce Development; he chairs the Congressional Equality Caucus.

As former Chairman of the Veterans' Affairs Committee, he authored the Honoring our PACT Act on toxic exposure, which according to his official biography expanded VA health care eligibility for over 3.5 million veterans exposed to burn pits.
